scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4673: The IT Department reports "switch0 (the IT-dept switch)
failed" -- they say the whole IT segment (192.168.1.0/24) is down because the
access switch connecting the IT hosts to their gateway stopped passing traffic, and
they want the switch replaced/restarted. Please confirm the switch failure.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The IT-segment switch is passing traffic: IT
  hosts (it_hod, it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach
  each other on 192.168.1.0/24. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of an L2 switch failure that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- the IT-dept switch (switch0)
failed and took down the IT segment -- is NOT reproducible: IT hosts (it_hod,
it_lab1-4) reach their gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss and reach each other across
192.168.1.0/24, which means the L2 switch is passing traffic normally.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the IT-segment switch is healthy and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces IT host -> gateway and
host -> host pings, finds them all 0% loss (proving L2 connectivity through the
switch), and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a failed switch -- declaring the
IT segment down to match the ticket -- is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The access switch for the IT segment (switch0) is operating normally. Multiple IT hosts (it_hod 192.168.1.2, it_lab1 .3, it_lab2 .4, it_lab3 .5, it_lab4 .6) have correct IP/gateway configuration and can reach their default gateway (router0 192.168.1.1) with 0% loss (e.g., it_lab1↔router0 round-trip <1 ms). They also have end-to-end reachability to other subnets: it_lab1 successfully pings office_pc (192.168.3.2), servers (1.0.0.5), and internet hosts (128.168.0.4) with 0% loss, indicating routing beyond the IT VLAN is intact.

On switch0, the Linux bridge br0 is UP with ports eth0 (uplink to router0) and eth1 (downlink to lan_it) in forwarding state. The bridge FDB shows learned MACs for all IT hosts on eth1 and the router’s MAC (46:b3:44:00:f5:ba) on eth0. Interface counters on eth0/eth1 show traffic flowing and zero errors/drops. Router0’s eth0 is UP as 192.168.1.1/24 and advertising/learning routes correctly.

Affected component: none; switching and L2 bridging are healthy.
Mechanism: Successful MAC learning and forwarding on br0; bidirectional ICMP across VLANs confirms L2/L3 paths.
Localization: switch0 br0 (eth0/eth1), router0 eth0, IT hosts.
Root cause: The reported “switch failure” is not present; the IT segment is up and passing traffic normally.
Corrective fix: No replacement or restart of switch0 is required. Close the ticket; if specific endpoints still report issues, investigate host NIC/cable or local software, and consider collecting timestamps/logs for any transient events.

per_axis.rationale: Agent confirmed IT hosts can reach the gateway with 0% loss but did not explicitly state that IT hosts reach each other on 192.168.1.0/24 with 0% loss.
